why: Code `eval` runs may run code in turn: here code in literal pieces, and code `sprintf` builds, each calling `f` twice (MATLAB doc 'eval'). Each call is a reference of its own, at its own place (step 14): where a piece writes its name, mapped through each literal around it, and, for the code `sprintf` builds, which no text written there spells, after the inner argument, mapped the same way. So with `lib/f.m` deleted, a fresh index keeps a failed row for each of the four calls, and so must a sync, and both link all four again when it is back (found by the step 14 second review: with a nested reference placed where its inner argument starts, the calls of one level shared one place, one edge, and one row after a sync).
